coordinates.note: The STRAW pathfinder paper (arXiv:1810.13265, P-ONE/Ocean Networks Canada authors) gives 47 deg 46 min N, 127 deg 46 min W (to 1 arcminute) for the ONC deep-sea infrastructure at the Cascadia Basin site, to which the STRAW pathfinder and P-ONE connect; that paper rounds the depth to about 2600 m, the 2021 site-characterization paper (arXiv:2108.04961) gives 2660 m (used for the depth value). It replaces an earlier coastal reference point (Barkley Sound, Vancouver Island, about 220 km away). The point is the position of the cabled site, not a surveyed seafloor mooring position, so it is marked approximate with a precision of 3 km that covers the arcminute rounding and the offset of the moorings from the node.
coordinates.quote: the ONC deep-sea infrastructure at Cascadia Basin dark site (47◦ 46’ N, 127◦ 46’ W), at a depth of ∼2600 m b.s.l.

depth.quote: An established ONC site, known as the Cascadia Basin (fig. 1), 2,660 m below sea level, provides an ideal environment for a large scale undersea neutrino telescope.

place.region: Cascadia Basin, off Vancouver Island, British Columbia

summary.plain: A deep patch of the Pacific Ocean floor off the west coast of Vancouver Island, Canada, more than 2.6 kilometres down, where a planned neutrino telescope will one day be built using an existing undersea cable network.
summary.technical: Cascadia Basin seafloor site on Ocean Networks Canada's NEPTUNE cabled observatory, 2660 m depth, roughly 200 km off the coast of Vancouver Island/British Columbia; coordinates (47°46'N, 127°46'W, to 1 arcminute) are the position the STRAW pathfinder paper gives for the Cascadia Basin site, not a surveyed seafloor mooring position.
